thread:
Ana (PM): Quick sync on rerank endpoint contract — customers are pushing for predictable top_k semantics, clear truncation rules, and an easy way to pass precomputed signals. Need a short proposal today.
Liam (Eng): +1. Can we list the knobs we need in the API first? top_k, normalization, truncation, and precomputed fields probably.
Meera (ML): From model side: normalization modes matter a lot for downstream stability. Suggest we support: none, softmax, minmax, zscore. Also allow clients to mark scores as already-normalized.
Oliver (SRE): Ops note: payload size and top_k affect memory/latency. We should set a safe default (top_k=10) and a hard cap (top_k<=200) for hosted tier. Dedicated can increase it by config.
Kai (Solutions): Customer feedback: 1) deterministic tie-breaking (some clients need stable order), 2) pagination for large candidate sets, 3) ability to send embeddings to avoid re-encoding.
Liam (Eng): Agree on determinism: tie-break by provided candidate_id, else input order. Pagination: server-side pagination increases complexity; prefer cursor-based cursors that encode last returned score + offset.
Meera (ML): Truncation discussion: do we truncate per-candidate or by overall token budget? Per-candidate token limit is simpler and clearer. Recommend default candidate_token_limit=1024, with explicit `truncate.mode` and `truncate.token_limit` in request.
Ana (PM): Draft API shape suggestion coming. Keep minimal for first launch, can expand later. Customers vs internal: which features are MVP vs later?
Liam (Eng): MVP: accept candidates array with {id, text, metadata, embedding? , raw_score?}, top_k, normalize enum, candidate_token_limit. Optional: precomputed embeddings and precomputed scores. No server pagination for MVP.
Meera (ML): Add a `normalize: 'none'|'softmax'|'minmax'|'zscore'` and `score_is_pre_normalized: boolean`. If precomputed embeddings provided, server should skip encoding.
Liam (Eng): Example request payload for API review: ```json
{
  "query": "best restaurants near me",
  "candidates": [
    {"id":"c1","text":"Pizza place...","metadata":{"rating":4.5}},
    {"id":"c2","text":"Sushi bar...","metadata":{}}
  ],
  "top_k": 10,
  "normalize": "softmax",
  "candidate_token_limit": 512,
  "deterministic_tiebreak": true
}
```
Kai (Solutions): Important: show customers how precomputed scores are treated. If they pass `raw_score` we should document whether we re-normalize or use as-is. Meera?
Meera (ML): We should re-normalize by default unless `score_is_pre_normalized=true`. Otherwise clients will get inconsistent results across methods. Also document numeric ranges we expect for raw_score.
Oliver (SRE): Rate limits and quota: larger candidate arrays are expensive. Recommend a soft limit of 500 candidates per request with clear error when exceeded. Also surface per-request estimated token cost in response metadata.
Ana (PM): Launch criteria checklist (proposal): 1) API shape settled + docs, 2) host default top_k and hard cap defined, 3) truncation and token limits documented, 4) normalization modes implemented + tests, 5) telemetry (latency + token cost) surfaced, 6) customer validation (2 pilot customers).
Liam (Eng): Implementation notes: we'll reuse the ranking infra but need an input validation pass for mixed embeddings+text, and a fast-path when embeddings provided. I'll sketch an RFC.
Meera (ML): Evaluation: add a regen test that verifies normalization parity across inputs and deterministic ordering with tie-break rule.
Kai (Solutions): I'll collect two customers willing to pilot precomputed embeddings and pagination needs.
DeployBot: New deploy scheduled: rerank-api-proto v0.1 -> staging at 1850001245 :rocket:
Ana (PM): Action items: @Liam draft RFC by EOD, @Meera write normalization doc fragment, @Kai onboard pilots. We'll reconvene tomorrow 11:00 to sign off on MVP. :thumbsup:
Liam (Eng): On it.
Meera (ML): Will do.
Kai (Solutions): Ping me if you want customer quotes.
Oliver (SRE): I'll add the hard cap and request size checks to the routing layer once we finalize numbers.
Ana (PM): Thanks all — we'll keep the shape conservative for launch and iterate.
